title: Metal Gear Acid 2
subtitle: A brighter look for a careful plan

body: Metal Gear Acid 2 is Konami's PSP tactical card game, first released in Japan on 8 December 2005. It continues Acid's alternate Metal Gear continuity, using cards to determine movement and actions during a turn-based stealth mission. A new cel-shaded presentation gives the sequel a much brighter appearance than its predecessor. The change is visual rather than a rejection of the central idea: the player still prepares a deck, reads the current hand and decides how to cross a guarded space with the resources that have become available.

New cover-fire behaviour allows an ally in a suitable position to support an attack, making coordination useful alongside the strength of an individual card. Surplus cards can be sold, giving deck management another way to improve the collection. Movement also becomes smoother around doors and items, reducing interruptions while retaining the turn-based decisions. The player has to think about where both characters stand before committing to a confrontation. A powerful card becomes more valuable when the surrounding positions allow the partner to contribute instead of leaving the attacker isolated.

The release included Solid Eye, a folding cardboard accessory whose lenses turn a divided PSP image into a stereoscopic view. It gives the game's unusual presentation a physical counterpart, inviting the player to look into the handheld differently. Shinta Nojiri returned as director, with music by Akihiro Honda, Hiroshi Tanabe and Nobuko Toda. Western editions followed in 2006. Acid 2 develops a small but distinctive branch of Metal Gear, combining familiar espionage imagery with deck construction, measured movement and an accessory unlike the ordinary equipment attached to a portable console.

Let the partner support the attack
A cardboard viewer adds another dimension
